Where it began

Wiaan Mulder was born in Johannesburg on 19 February 1998 and went to school at St Stithians College. Gauteng picked him for its age-group sides all the way from the under-13s, and was part of South Africa's squad at the 2016 Under-19 World Cup.

That October, before he had even left school, he made his first-class debut for the Highveld Lions against Cape Cobras at The Wanderers. He took seven wickets in the match, including 3 for 10 in the first innings, which is not a bad way to spend a school term.

The player

His first one-day international came against Bangladesh in October 2017, and his Test debut against Sri Lanka in 2019. He built a steady career as a batting all-rounder who could bowl seam. By November 2026 he had played 28 Tests, scoring 1,440 runs at 35.12 with four hundreds, taking 48 wickets at 26.81 with a best of 4 for 32, and holding 35 catches.

The hundreds tell a story of their own. His first, 105 not out, came against Bangladesh in October 2024. In June 2025 he made 147 against Zimbabwe at Bulawayo. Then, handed the captaincy for the second Test of that series, he made 367 not out, by November 2026 the highest Test score by a South African and by any captain, before declaring the innings closed. He was also part of the side that won the 2025 World Test Championship final.

What made him special

He was the sort of all-rounder who made a team easier to pick: runs in the middle order, overs when needed and safe hands in the field. When he settled in, he tended to stay. Four of his five Test innings past fifty went on to three figures, which suggests he thought of fifty as a stop on the way rather than a destination.

The declaration at 367 summed him up. He was only 33 runs short of Brian Lara's 400 not out, and said afterwards that he had not wanted to take the record from a player he admired so much.

Away from the middle

English county cricket knew him well. He turned out for Kent in 2019 and for Leicestershire in 2021 and 2022, and for Leicestershire in July 2022 he made his first double hundred in first-class cricket, 235 not out. At home he played for the Lions and for Gauteng.

And finally

By November 2026 he had captained South Africa in a single Test and won it, which made for a perfect record as captain. Few leaders can say that, and he made 367 along the way.
